detailed_rationale:
Zensar Technologies is a Pune-based, RPG-Group digital and IT services company organized around Application Management and Infrastructure Management Services, with vertical concentration in hi-tech/manufacturing, consumer services and BFSI, and geographic exposure to the US, UK, Europe and Africa. The recent quarterly trend is steadily positive: sales have risen from Rs.1,308 Cr (Sep-2024) to Rs.1,508 Cr (Jun-2026), roughly 9% YoY, with net profit recovering in tandem from Rs.156 Cr to Rs.184-211 Cr over the same run, and EPS climbing from Rs.6.86 to Rs.9.26 at the Q4 FY26 peak. The balance sheet is a genuine strength - the company has reduced debt and is almost debt-free, working capital days have improved from 25.7 to 19.9, and dividend payout is healthy at 40% of profits, alongside an 18.2% 5-year profit CAGR that has outpaced revenue growth (~8.5% 5-year), implying real margin/efficiency gains rather than one-off items - other income (TTM ~Rs.210 Cr) looks like a stable treasury yield off the debt-free cash pile rather than a distorting one-off.

Shareholding shows FIIs trimming (from ~16.7% to ~10.7% over the last several quarters) while DIIs have added (~15.5% to ~24%) - a rotation pattern common in mid-cap IT during global EM-flow adjustments, not in itself a governance flag, and promoter holding is rock-stable at ~49% with no pledge disclosed. One item worth flagging for completeness: the FY27 AGM (Jul-2026) approved a large (~Rs.750 Cr) related-party transaction, and the US subsidiary Bridgeview Life Sciences was merged into Zensar Technologies Inc. effective Aug-2026 - both look like routine intra-group/subsidiary housekeeping for an RPG-group company rather than anything adversarial, but they are the kind of items an analyst should keep on a watchlist rather than wave through unread.

Valuation is undemanding: at a stock PE of ~14.7-15.6x against a business compounding profit at high-teens over five years and improving working-capital efficiency, the multiple is closer to cheap than rich for the quality on offer, though IT-services growth remains subject to constant-currency/GenAI-pricing risk industry-wide that could compress multiples further if deal-TCV momentum stalls.
recommendation_rationale: The quant score already reads Hold on both the 3-year and 1-year lens, driven by a moderate quality score and a high value score (cheap PE). My own read agrees: steady high-single-digit growth, an 18% profit CAGR, a debt-free balance sheet and a sub-16x multiple do not support a Sell, and there is no analytical tension pulling the other way (no override, no escalation) - Hold is the correct call as-is.
summary: Zensar Technologies is a mid-cap IT services company (part of the RPG Group) with steady mid-to-high single-digit revenue growth, improving profitability, and a debt-free balance sheet. The stock trades at a reasonable valuation relative to its growth and quality, so we rate it a Hold: no fresh reason to exit, but also no standout re-rating trigger visible today.
positive_para: Zensar has compounded profit at 18.2% annually over five years even as revenue grew a more modest ~8.5%, evidence of genuine margin and working-capital discipline (WC days down from 25.7 to 19.9), and the balance sheet is debt-free with a healthy 40% dividend payout. The recent quarterly run shows accelerating profit (Rs.156 Cr to Rs.211 Cr net profit over roughly two years) alongside a still-modest ~15x PE - cheap enough that continued execution could support a re-rating, and DII buying suggests domestic institutional confidence even as FIIs have trimmed.
negative_para: The five-year sales growth of ~8.5% is genuinely unexciting for an IT services business and leaves limited room for error if deal wins slow; FII holding has fallen meaningfully (roughly 16.7% to 10.7% over the last several quarters), and while that can reflect broader EM-flow rotation rather than company-specific concern, it is a real reduction in a historically supportive holder base. The ~Rs.750 Cr FY27 related-party transaction approved at the AGM and the US subsidiary merger are routine-looking but add a layer of intra-group complexity worth monitoring, and like the rest of mid-cap IT, Zensar's growth remains exposed to GenAI-driven pricing compression and constant-currency softness that headline sales numbers can mask.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At ~15x earnings against an 18% five-year profit CAGR and improving capital efficiency, the multiple implies the market expects only modest continuation of recent growth, not acceleration - a fair-to-slightly-cheap price for a debt-free, steadily-compounding mid-cap IT services franchise. Growth is well below the 25% hypergrowth threshold, so no dilution/ROE-tier note applies.
